tools.name: explain_brex
tools.description: List the rules of a BREX data module in readable form: for each rule, the target (XPath), whether it is forbidden / required / optional, the allowed values with their meanings, severity, and the schema context it applies to. Also returns the BREX header (DMC, parent BREX, commonInfo, counts). Use "kind" and "context" to narrow, "offset"/"limit" to page. The header carries the whole commonInfo text whatever "limit" is; pass includeCommonInfo: false to get its length instead.

brex.description: Which BREX to use: a file path to a BREX data module (.xml), or a DMC (e.g. "KENBAIKI-A-00-00-00-00A-022A-D", "DMC-" prefix optional) searched in csdbDirs / S1000D_CSDB_DIR / S1000D_SPEC_DIR. Omit to use the S1000D default BREX found under S1000D_SPEC_DIR.

csdbDirs.description: CSDB folders to search for BREX by DMC (default: S1000D_CSDB_DIR / the config file; S1000D_SPEC_DIR is always searched for the S1000D default BREX). When given, these folders replace S1000D_CSDB_DIR and the csdbDirs of the config file (they are not added to them); folders that do not exist are skipped and reported in _notes.

context.description: Only rules that apply to this schema (file name such as "descript", "proced", "pm") plus the common rules. Omit for all contexts.

search.description: Case-insensitive text to find in objectPath, objectUse, rule id or value meanings.

offset.description: Index of the first rule to return (default 0).

includeCommonInfo.description: Return the commonInfo text of the BREX in the header (default true). Pass false to get "commonInfoLength" (number of characters) instead, for example when reading further pages of the same BREX.

tools.name: lookup_sns
tools.description: Explain what a Standard Numbering System (SNS) code means in a BREX: pass a DMC (the system / subsystem / sub-subsystem / assembly codes are taken from it) or the codes directly. Returns the matched hierarchy with titles; "exact: false" means only a prefix matched.

brex.description: Which BREX to use: a file path to a BREX data module (.xml), or a DMC (e.g. "KENBAIKI-A-00-00-00-00A-022A-D", "DMC-" prefix optional) searched in csdbDirs / S1000D_CSDB_DIR / S1000D_SPEC_DIR. Omit to use the S1000D default BREX found under S1000D_SPEC_DIR.

csdbDirs.description: CSDB folders to search for BREX by DMC (default: S1000D_CSDB_DIR / the config file; S1000D_SPEC_DIR is always searched for the S1000D default BREX). When given, these folders replace S1000D_CSDB_DIR and the csdbDirs of the config file (they are not added to them); folders that do not exist are skipped and reported in _notes.

dmc.description: A DMC whose SNS part should be looked up.

systemCode.description: System code (2-3 characters), when not passing dmc.

tools.name: lookup_value
tools.description: Explain what a value of an element or attribute means in a BREX, or list the allowed values. Pass "target" as an attribute name (e.g. "securityClassification"), an element name, or an XPath fragment; optionally "value" to check one value. Returns the matching rules with allowed values and their meanings, and whether the value is allowed.

brex.description: Which BREX to use: a file path to a BREX data module (.xml), or a DMC (e.g. "KENBAIKI-A-00-00-00-00A-022A-D", "DMC-" prefix optional) searched in csdbDirs / S1000D_CSDB_DIR / S1000D_SPEC_DIR. Omit to use the S1000D default BREX found under S1000D_SPEC_DIR.

csdbDirs.description: CSDB folders to search for BREX by DMC (default: S1000D_CSDB_DIR / the config file; S1000D_SPEC_DIR is always searched for the S1000D default BREX). When given, these folders replace S1000D_CSDB_DIR and the csdbDirs of the config file (they are not added to them); folders that do not exist are skipped and reported in _notes.

target.description: Attribute name ("infoCode", "@infoCode"), element name ("language"), or XPath fragment to match against objectPath.

value.description: The value to check against the allowed values (optional).

context.description: Schema file name (e.g. "descript") to pick context-specific rules in addition to common ones.

tools.name: list_notations
tools.description: List the illustration / multimedia notations (file formats) a BREX allows: the base set (common to all schemas) and the per-schema additions and exclusions. Pass "context" to get the effective rule for one schema: mode "closed" (only the listed notations may be used), "open" (only the excluded ones are forbidden; a BREX with exclusions only) or "unrestricted". Returns an empty base set when the BREX has no notation rules (then the BREX does not restrict notations).

brex.description: Which BREX to use: a file path to a BREX data module (.xml), or a DMC (e.g. "KENBAIKI-A-00-00-00-00A-022A-D", "DMC-" prefix optional) searched in csdbDirs / S1000D_CSDB_DIR / S1000D_SPEC_DIR. Omit to use the S1000D default BREX found under S1000D_SPEC_DIR.

csdbDirs.description: CSDB folders to search for BREX by DMC (default: S1000D_CSDB_DIR / the config file; S1000D_SPEC_DIR is always searched for the S1000D default BREX). When given, these folders replace S1000D_CSDB_DIR and the csdbDirs of the config file (they are not added to them); folders that do not exist are skipped and reported in _notes.

context.description: Schema file name (e.g. "ipd", "proced") to compute the effective set for.

tools.name: check_against_brex
tools.description: Check a data module against BREX rules and report violations with location (XPath + line), actual value, rule id, objectUse text and severity. Also accepts a publication module (pm) or a comment (the brexDmRef in pmStatus / commentStatus is followed). By default follows the document's brexDmRef chain (project BREX → … → the BREX that ends the chain by referring to itself: usually the S1000D default BREX found under S1000D_SPEC_DIR) and checks each layer separately; pass "brex" to check against one specific BREX instead or in addition. Does NOT validate against the XML schema (XSD): run schema validation separately. nonContextRules cannot be checked automatically and are returned as manualChecks.

path.description: File path of the data module to check.

xml.description: The data module as an XML string (alternative to path; max 5 MB).

brex.description: A specific BREX (file path or DMC) to check against. With followChain=false it is the only layer; otherwise it is added to the chain.

followChain.description: Follow the brexDmRef chain of the data module (default true).

csdbDirs.description: CSDB folders to search for BREX by DMC (default: S1000D_CSDB_DIR / the config file; S1000D_SPEC_DIR is always searched for the S1000D default BREX). When given, these folders replace S1000D_CSDB_DIR and the csdbDirs of the config file (they are not added to them); folders that do not exist are skipped and reported in _notes.

includeManualChecks.description: Include nonContextRules as manualChecks in each layer (default true).

maxViolationsPerLayer.description: Cap on violations returned per layer (default 200). The total count is always reported.

tools.name: verify_data_module
tools.description: Verify one S1000D data module: well-formedness, XML schema (XSD) validation against the user's own S1000D schemas (S1000D_SPEC_DIR), BREX checks along the brexDmRef chain, and reference resolution (dmRef, pmRef, ICN entities, internalRef, applicRefId). Returns a "verification" status (the same VerificationStatus that s1000d-reader-mcp embeds) plus the details of each step. Does NOT decide S1000D conformance.

path.description: File path of the data module (or PM) to check.

xml.description: The document as an XML string (alternative to path; max 5 MB).

csdbDirs.description: CSDB folders to search for referenced data modules, publication modules, ICN files and BREX (default: S1000D_CSDB_DIR / the config file; BREX is also searched under S1000D_SPEC_DIR). When given, these folders replace S1000D_CSDB_DIR and the csdbDirs of the config file (they are not added to them); folders that do not exist are skipped and reported in _notes.

skip.description: Steps to skip. Skipped steps are reported with state "not-run".

maxSchemaErrors.description: Cap on XSD errors returned (default 100). The total count is always reported.

maxViolationsPerLayer.description: Cap on BREX violations returned per layer (default 200).

tools.name: validate_schema
tools.description: Validate one document against the S1000D XML schema (XSD) named by its xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation. The XSD is taken from the xml_schema_flat/ folder found under S1000D_SPEC_DIR (the issue is read from brex.xsd there). Errors are libxml2 messages with line/column. Returns schema-not-found with a reason when no suitable XSD is available.

path.description: File path of the data module (or PM) to check.

xml.description: The document as an XML string (alternative to path; max 5 MB).

issue.description: S1000D issue of the XSD to use when several xml_schema_flat/ folders exist (e.g. "7", "4.2"). Default: inferred from the schemaLocation URL.

tools.name: check_references
tools.description: List the references of one document and whether each target exists: dmRef (all contexts: brexDmRef, applicCrossRefTableRef, pmEntry, body), pmRef, ICN (graphic/@infoEntityIdent via the DOCTYPE ENTITY declaration to a file), internalRef (ids in the same document) and applicRefId (applic ids or referencedApplicGroupRef/applicRef). Unresolved references carry a reason (not-found, no-entity-declaration, file-not-found, no-such-id, no-csdb). dmRef to modelIdentCode "S1000D" point to the specification itself and are listed separately.

path.description: File path of the data module (or PM) to check.

xml.description: The document as an XML string (alternative to path; max 5 MB).

csdbDirs.description: CSDB folders to search for referenced data modules, publication modules, ICN files and BREX (default: S1000D_CSDB_DIR / the config file; BREX is also searched under S1000D_SPEC_DIR). When given, these folders replace S1000D_CSDB_DIR and the csdbDirs of the config file (they are not added to them); folders that do not exist are skipped and reported in _notes.

includeResolved.description: Also list resolved references with the file they resolve to (default false; counts are always returned).

tools.name: verify_csdb
tools.description: Verify every CSDB object (data modules by default; optionally publication modules etc.) found in the given folders, and return one VerificationStatus per object plus totals (valid / XSD errors / BREX violations / unresolved references / unreadable). Use offset/limit to page. Pass reportPath to also write the full JSON report to a file.

csdbDirs.description: Folders to verify (default: S1000D_CSDB_DIR / the config file). Referenced objects are also searched here. When given, these folders replace S1000D_CSDB_DIR and the csdbDirs of the config file (they are not added to them); folders that do not exist are skipped and reported in _notes.

include.description: Object kinds to verify (default: dm and pm).

skip.description: Steps to skip. Skipped steps are reported with state "not-run".

reportPath.description: If given, the full report (all details) is written to this JSON file; the response keeps only the statuses.

tools.name: suggest_fixes
tools.description: Verify one data module (same steps as verify_data_module) and return fix candidates for each finding: XSD errors (values and elements from the libxml2 message or from the XSD definitions), BREX violations (the rule's allowed values with their descriptions; remove / add for forbidden / missing; allowed notations), unresolved references (similar DMCs in the CSDB, the issue present in the CSDB, ICN files that differ only in the extension, similar ids) and, when "product" is given, applicability that cannot be decided because the product lacks a value (values from the ACT, CCT and PCT). Every candidate is decided by the server; each fix has a confidence (exact / several / none) and the source of its candidates. Does NOT apply any fix.

path.description: File path of the data module (or PM) to check.

xml.description: The document as an XML string (alternative to path; max 5 MB).

csdbDirs.description: CSDB folders to search for referenced data modules, publication modules, ICN files and BREX (default: S1000D_CSDB_DIR / the config file; BREX is also searched under S1000D_SPEC_DIR). When given, these folders replace S1000D_CSDB_DIR and the csdbDirs of the config file (they are not added to them); folders that do not exist are skipped and reported in _notes.

skip.description: Steps to skip. Skipped steps are reported with state "not-run".

product.description: The product to evaluate applicability against. If given, applicability that is undetermined because the product lacks a value is reported with candidate values. Omit it to skip applicability.

includeSpecificationReferences.description: Also list fixes for dmRef to the S1000D specification itself (modelIdentCode "S1000D"). They are never in a CSDB, are not errors and carry no candidate (default false; the count is always returned).

maxFixes.description: Cap on fixes returned (default 200). The total count is always reported.

maxCandidates.description: Cap on candidates per fix (default 20). A fix that was cut carries candidateCount.

tools.name: reconcile_dml
tools.description: Reconcile a data module list (DML) or a data dispatch note (DDN) with the CSDB. For each DML entry (dmRef / pmRef / infoEntityRef / dmlRef) or DDN delivery item (dispatchFileName) it reports found / issue-mismatch (the object exists but not the issue the list names; the latest issue in the CSDB is given) / not-found / not-checked (commentRef), plus the data modules and publication modules that are in the CSDB but not listed in the DML (notListed, each with the issue of the file as issueInfo; limited to the model identification codes that appear in the DML). Pass path or xml of one DML or DDN; omit both to reconcile every DML and DDN found in the CSDB folders. The values of dmlType / dmlEntryType / issueType are returned as in the XSD enumerations, without interpretation.

path.description: File path of the DML or DDN. Omit path and xml to reconcile every DML and DDN in the CSDB.

xml.description: The DML or DDN as an XML string (alternative to path; max 5 MB).

csdbDirs.description: CSDB folders to search for referenced data modules, publication modules, ICN files and BREX (default: S1000D_CSDB_DIR / the config file; BREX is also searched under S1000D_SPEC_DIR). When given, these folders replace S1000D_CSDB_DIR and the csdbDirs of the config file (they are not added to them); folders that do not exist are skipped and reported in _notes.

includeFound.description: Also list the entries whose state is "found" (default false: only issue-mismatch / not-found / not-checked are listed; counts always cover everything).

includeNotListed.description: Report CSDB objects that the DML does not list (default true).

maxItems.description: Maximum entries and notListed objects to return per list (default 200, max 5000).

tools.name: list_schemas
tools.description: Show which S1000D XML schema folders (xml_schema_flat/ containing brex.xsd) were found under S1000D_SPEC_DIR, with the issue read from brex.xsd and the schema names available. Use it to diagnose schema-not-found results.

tools.name: list_data_modules
tools.description: List the CSDB objects (data modules by default; optionally publication modules, DML, DDN, IMF, UPF, ICN) in the CSDB folders with DMC parts, techName/infoName, issue, language, schema name (descript/proced/…), S1000D issue and applicability display text. A DML or DDN row also carries its code, issue date, entry/item count and a reconciliation summary against the CSDB (found / issue-mismatch / not-found / not-checked; for a DML also how many DMs and PMs it does not list). Filter by modelIdentCode, systemCode, infoCode, schemaName or title text. Paged with offset/limit.

csdbDirs.description: CSDB folders to search for data modules by DMC, referenced objects, ACT/CCT/PCT and BREX (default: S1000D_CSDB_DIR / the config file). When given, these folders replace S1000D_CSDB_DIR and the csdbDirs of the config file (they are not added to them); folders that do not exist are skipped and reported in _notes.

schemaName.description: descript / proced / process / fault / pm / brex / …

text.description: Case-insensitive text to find in techName or infoName.

tools.name: read_data_module
tools.description: Read one data module as structure, not XML: identification and status (DMC, issue, language, title, BREX ref, QA, DM-level applicability), the body as a tree of blocks (sections, paragraphs, lists, tables, figures with ICN, warnings/cautions/notes, numbered steps, requirements; processes and fault isolation too), the references it makes, ALWAYS a "verification" status (XSD by default) and ALWAYS "securityClassification" (the data module's value and the values carried by elements in the body, uninterpreted) at the top of the response. section "outline" returns a summary (headings, step numbers, first sentence, size of each subtree) for deciding what to read. Applicability of each block is evaluated for the given product (applicable / notApplicable / undetermined); without a product, only display texts are returned — assert expressions are never returned.

xml.description: The document as an XML string (alternative to path; max 5 MB).

dmc.description: DMC of the data module to read from the CSDB (e.g. "S1000DBIKE-AAA-D00-00-00-00AA-041A-A"; "DMC-" prefix optional). Alternative to path/xml.

csdbDirs.description: CSDB folders to search for data modules by DMC, referenced objects, ACT/CCT/PCT and BREX (default: S1000D_CSDB_DIR / the config file). When given, these folders replace S1000D_CSDB_DIR and the csdbDirs of the config file (they are not added to them); folders that do not exist are skipped and reported in _notes.

product.description: The product to evaluate applicability for. attributes: ACT productAttribute id → value (e.g. {"model": "Brook trekker", "version": "Mk9"}); conditions: CCT cond id → value. Omit to get "undetermined" with display texts only. Use describe_applicability to learn the available ids and values.

section.description: Which part to return (default all). "outline" returns only headings, step numbers, the first sentence and the size (nodes / chars / admonitions) of each subtree — call it first on a large data module to decide what to read.

includeLocation.description: Add "location" (path, line, column) to every node of the body or the outline (default false). Pass true when you are going to edit the data module with s1000d-writer-mcp edit_data_module: its "at" and "to" take location.path as returned here. With section "content" or "all", a step also gets "textLocations": the locations of the paragraphs joined into its "text", in order. The outline has no textLocations.

outlineDepth.description: With section "outline": how many levels of headings / steps to return (default: all levels).

verify.description: How much to verify before reading: "schema" (default) runs XSD validation only; "full" also checks BREX along the brexDmRef chain and resolves references; "none" skips verification (reported as not-run).

omitNotApplicable.description: Drop blocks that are notApplicable for the given product (default false: keep them, marked). The number dropped is reported.

tools.name: read_publication_module
tools.description: Read a publication module (PMC) as a table of contents: the pmEntry tree with titles, and for each dmRef/pmRef the resolved target (file, techName/infoName, issue) from the CSDB. Also returns the PM identification and a verification status.

xml.description: The document as an XML string (alternative to path; max 5 MB).

pmc.description: PMC to read from the CSDB (e.g. "S1000DBIKE-B6865-EPWG1-00"; "PMC-" prefix optional). Alternative to path/xml.

csdbDirs.description: CSDB folders to search for data modules by DMC, referenced objects, ACT/CCT/PCT and BREX (default: S1000D_CSDB_DIR / the config file). When given, these folders replace S1000D_CSDB_DIR and the csdbDirs of the config file (they are not added to them); folders that do not exist are skipped and reported in _notes.

verify.description: How much to verify before reading: "schema" (default) runs XSD validation only; "full" also checks BREX along the brexDmRef chain and resolves references; "none" skips verification (reported as not-run).

tools.name: resolve_reference
tools.description: Resolve one reference to a CSDB object: a DMC, a PMC, or an ICN (file name or entity name). Returns the file path(s), issue(s) and title. For an ICN, pass "fromPath" of the data module whose DOCTYPE declares the entity to get the declared file and notation.

icn.description: ICN (entity name or file name) to resolve.

fromPath.description: Data module whose DOCTYPE declares the ICN entity (optional).

csdbDirs.description: CSDB folders to search for data modules by DMC, referenced objects, ACT/CCT/PCT and BREX (default: S1000D_CSDB_DIR / the config file). When given, these folders replace S1000D_CSDB_DIR and the csdbDirs of the config file (they are not added to them); folders that do not exist are skipped and reported in _notes.

tools.name: describe_applicability
tools.description: Describe the applicability vocabulary of a data module so a product can be chosen: the ACT product attributes (ids, names, enumerations/patterns, which one identifies the product), the CCT condition types and conditions, the PCT products (ready-made product values), the applic statements in the data module (ids and display texts), and which attributes used by the statements have no value in the PCT. Nothing is evaluated here; pass the chosen values as "product" to read_data_module.

xml.description: The document as an XML string (alternative to path; max 5 MB).

dmc.description: DMC of the data module to read from the CSDB (e.g. "S1000DBIKE-AAA-D00-00-00-00AA-041A-A"; "DMC-" prefix optional). Alternative to path/xml.

csdbDirs.description: CSDB folders to search for data modules by DMC, referenced objects, ACT/CCT/PCT and BREX (default: S1000D_CSDB_DIR / the config file). When given, these folders replace S1000D_CSDB_DIR and the csdbDirs of the config file (they are not added to them); folders that do not exist are skipped and reported in _notes.

tools.name: read_icn_metadata
tools.description: Read an ICN metadata file (IMF, icnmetadata.xsd): ICN, issue, title, keywords, security, source/originator and other status items as a flat list, plus the related ICN files found in the CSDB.

xml.description: The document as an XML string (alternative to path; max 5 MB).

icn.description: ICN whose IMF to read from the CSDB (e.g. "C0419-S1000D0360-001-01" or "ICN-C0419-…").

csdbDirs.description: CSDB folders to search for data modules by DMC, referenced objects, ACT/CCT/PCT and BREX (default: S1000D_CSDB_DIR / the config file). When given, these folders replace S1000D_CSDB_DIR and the csdbDirs of the config file (they are not added to them); folders that do not exist are skipped and reported in _notes.

tools.name: build_data_module
tools.description: Build ONE S1000D data module (descript / proced / process / fault) or publication module (pm) from a structured draft and number it from the allocation rules. You give titles, paragraphs, steps, tables, figures and references as a tree; the server writes the XML (you never write XML, DMCs, ICNs or the BREX reference). The XML is verified (XSD, BREX along the brexDmRef chain, references; applicability too when a product is given); fixes the server is certain about (confidence "exact") are applied automatically and verified again, up to maxFixRounds times. Returns xml, fileName, dmCode (pmCode for a pm), verification, appliedFixes[] (what was changed automatically), fixes[] (what remains: candidates to choose from), the updated ledger and the next ICN number. Writes into the CSDB only when write is true. A malformed draft comes back as error.code "input-error" with the path of the problem; a draft without applic is one (path "/applic"): the server does not decide applicability, so give at least applic.displayText.

draft.description: The data module as a tree. kind decides which node kinds are accepted.

sourceId.description: 採番に使う識別子。dmCode（pm は pmCode）を省いたときに要る。同じ sourceId には同じ DMC を返す

issueDate.description: YYYY-MM-DD。省略時は実行環境の今日の日付

securityClassification.description: 機密区分（列挙のまま。省略を許さない）

responsiblePartnerCompany.description: 責任企業の企業コード。省略時は allocation.icn.cageCode

originator.description: 作成者の企業コード。省略時は allocation.icn.cageCode

allocation.description: Numbering rules and the ledger. Pass the ledger of the previous response back so that the same sourceId keeps the same DMC and the same asset keeps the same ICN.

map.description: sourceId → DMC の一部。無い sourceId は rules で決める

disassyCode.description: 指定すると分解コードを連番にしない

infoCodeByKind.description: kind ごとの情報コード。既定は無く、省略した kind を採番すると入力の誤りになる

cageCode.description: ICN の CAGE コード

next.description: 次に使う連番。応答に次の値を返す

ledger.description: sourceId → DMC / PMC、assetId → ICN。前回の応答の ledger をそのまま渡す

csdbDirs.description: CSDB folders used to resolve references, find BREX and number new objects (default: S1000D_CSDB_DIR / the config file). The FIRST folder is also where write: true writes (it may not exist yet). When given, these folders replace S1000D_CSDB_DIR and the csdbDirs of the config file (they are not added to them); other folders that do not exist are skipped and reported in _notes.

write.description: Write the result into the CSDB (the first folder of csdbDirs / S1000D_CSDB_DIR). Default false: the XML is only returned. Nothing is written when the XML is not valid against the XSD unless allowInvalid is true.

overwrite.description: With write: true, replace a file of the same name. Default false: an existing file is left alone and reported as write-conflict.

allowInvalid.description: With write: true, write even when verification.schema.state is "invalid". Default false.

maxFixRounds.description: How many times to apply the fixes the server is certain about (confidence "exact") and verify again (default 3). 0 turns automatic fixing off.

maxFixes.description: Cap on the remaining fixes listed in the response (default 50).

product.description: The product to evaluate applicability for. attributes: ACT productAttribute id → value; conditions: CCT cond id → value. Omit to skip the applicability check.

issuePolicy.description: When the CSDB already has the same data module and the draft gives no issueInfo: raise issueNumber (default), raise inWork, or keep the issue.

assetFormats.description: File format of each figure original, by assetId (or ICN): { extension: "PNG", notation: "png", publicId? }. Default: taken from the original file name for known formats (png, jpg, gif, svg, cgm, pdf).

tools.name: convert_manual
tools.description: Convert an experiential operation manual (@shuji-bonji/experiential-manual-model JSON) into S1000D: one publication module, one data module per topic (description → descript, procedure → proced, troubleshooting → fault, screenFlow → process plus one proced per screen), a glossary data module, applicability from the scopes, and ICNs for the assets. Every data module goes through the same flow as build_data_module (build, verify, automatic exact fixes, verify again); references between the data modules are resolved against the CSDB plus the data modules built in this call. A topic whose prerequisites list an item without an identifier (natoStockNumber or manufacturerCode) or without quantity is not built (its dataModules[] row carries error.code "input-error" and the path of the item; leaving the item out would write noSupplies, which reads as "nothing is required"); the other data modules are still built. Returns dataModules[], publicationModule, assets[] (assetId → ICN and the original file; with write: true the originals are copied under the ICN file name), the ledger, a summary of verification states and notRepresented (what the draft format cannot express). Nothing is written unless write is true.

tools.name: apply_fixes
tools.description: Apply fixes to an existing data module. Each selection copies the location and ONE candidate of a fix that s1000d-verify-mcp suggest_fixes (or this server) returned: { location, action, target?, value?, position? }. The server computes the fix candidates again and applies a selection only if it matches one of them; a value outside the candidates (or outside a range / pattern candidate) is not applied and comes back in rejected[] with the reason. "provide" candidates change the product, not the document: pass them as "product". The result is verified again. Returns xml, applied[], rejected[], verification, the fixes that remain. Writes only when write is true (a path is overwritten in place; xml is written under its own file name in the first CSDB folder).

xml.description: An existing document as an XML string (alternative to path; max 5 MB). Not for XML you wrote yourself: build new data modules with build_data_module.

csdbDirs.description: CSDB folders used to resolve references, find BREX and number new objects (default: S1000D_CSDB_DIR / the config file). The FIRST folder is also where write: true writes (it may not exist yet). When given, these folders replace S1000D_CSDB_DIR and the csdbDirs of the config file (they are not added to them); other folders that do not exist are skipped and reported in _notes.

location.description: Fix.location of the suggestion (omit when the fix has none, e.g. a missing element).

position.description: Copy it when the candidate has "position" (an element added before the one at the location). Without it the selection does not match that candidate.

product.description: The product to evaluate applicability for. attributes: ACT productAttribute id → value; conditions: CCT cond id → value. Omit to skip the applicability check.

write.description: Write the result into the CSDB (the first folder of csdbDirs / S1000D_CSDB_DIR). Default false: the XML is only returned. Nothing is written when the XML is not valid against the XSD unless allowInvalid is true.

overwrite.description: With write: true, replace a file of the same name. Default false: an existing file is left alone and reported as write-conflict.

allowInvalid.description: With write: true, write even when verification.schema.state is "invalid". Default false.

maxFixes.description: Cap on the remaining fixes listed in the response (default 50).

tools.name: edit_data_module
tools.description: Change the structure of an EXISTING procedural or descriptive data module: insert a node, remove a node, move a node. Places are location.path values of the document as it is now (s1000d-reader-mcp read_data_module returns them); with several edits, every place still refers to the document before any edit. A node to insert is a structured draft node (step / para / admonition / listItem), never XML. All edits are applied or none: refusals[] gives the reason per edit (for example id-referenced, not-allowed-here, unsupported-node, released-issue). Only the edited ranges of the original text are rewritten; the rest stays character for character, and a moved element keeps its content unchanged. Elements that can be removed or moved: proceduralStep, para, warning, caution, note, listItem. Without "marking" this tool does NOT change the issue information or add change markup (changeType, changeMark, reasonForUpdate): a released issue (inWork "00") is refused unless allowReleasedIssue is true. With "marking" it adds change markup on an IN-WORK issue (start one with start_revision): an inserted node gets changeType="add"; a removed node is KEPT and gets changeType="delete" (changes[].kept); a move is accepted only within the same parent, which gets changeType="modify"; edits inside an element already marked add or delete get no markup; reasonForUpdate tells which reason the markup refers to. The result is verified again; XSD errors that the edits introduced come back in newSchemaErrors[] and such a result is never written. Returns applied, xml (unless includeXml is false), changes[] (each with mark when change markup was added), reasonForUpdate (with marking), refusals[], newSchemaErrors[], referencedFromOtherObjects[], verification, fixes[] (without candidates for the new XSD errors: change the edits and call again instead). Writes only when write is true (a path is overwritten in place).

csdbDirs.description: CSDB folders used to resolve references, find BREX and number new objects (default: S1000D_CSDB_DIR / the config file). The FIRST folder is also where write: true writes (it may not exist yet). When given, these folders replace S1000D_CSDB_DIR and the csdbDirs of the config file (they are not added to them); other folders that do not exist are skipped and reported in _notes.

to.description: insert / move: location.path of the reference node (the node beside or inside which the node goes).

position.description: insert / move: before / after the reference node, or as the first / last child of it. The XSD fixes the order of children (in a proceduralStep: warnings and cautions, then paragraphs, then nested steps); a wrong order comes back in newSchemaErrors[].

tools.name: start_revision
tools.description: Start an in-work issue of a RELEASED data module (issueInfo/@inWork "00") so that it can be changed by the S1000D rules. The result is a NEW document: issueNumber unchanged, inWork "01", issueType as given; the released issue is never changed. The change markup of the previous issue is removed (changeType / changeMark / reasonForUpdateRefIds, changeInline tags with their text kept, every reasonForUpdate) and elements marked changeType="delete" are removed; only those ranges of the original text are rewritten. issueType is REQUIRED and is the user's decision: "changed" (changes shown with change markup: then edit with edit_data_module marking), "revised" (reworked, no change markup), "status" (only the identification and status section), "new" only when starting from issue 001-00. Optional "reason" adds one reasonForUpdate to the in-work issue in the same call (with revised or status from issue 002 on, the default BREX requires one). Refused: a document already in work, a deleted issue, an id of a removed element that the rest still refers to. Not done: release (inWork back to "00", issueNumber + 1), issueDate, quality assurance. Returns started, xml (unless includeXml is false), previous, issueInfo, issueType, fileName, removed{}, reasonForUpdate, refusals[], newSchemaErrors[], referencedFromOtherObjects[], verification, fixes[]. With write: true the in-work issue is written under fileName beside "path" (or into the CSDB when xml was given); an existing file of that name is a write-conflict.

xml.description: An existing document as an XML string (alternative to path; max 5 MB). Not for XML you wrote yourself: build new data modules with build_data_module.

csdbDirs.description: CSDB folders used to resolve references, find BREX and number new objects (default: S1000D_CSDB_DIR / the config file). The FIRST folder is also where write: true writes (it may not exist yet). When given, these folders replace S1000D_CSDB_DIR and the csdbDirs of the config file (they are not added to them); other folders that do not exist are skipped and reported in _notes.

issueType.description: issueType of the in-work issue. Ask the user; it is never chosen for you. "new" is accepted only when starting from 001-00 (it follows Chap 3.9.5.1 Table 3 but the default BREX reports BREX-S1-00030).

reason.description: Optional: one reason for update to add to the in-work issue (same as add_reason_for_update). If it cannot be added, the in-work issue is not started either.

text.description: The text of the reason (one simplePara).

updateReasonType.description: S1000D updateReasonType, written as given: urt01 editorial change (no change markup may refer to it), urt02 technical change, urt03 markup only, urt04 applicability only, urt05 references only; urt51-urt99 are project values. Required: it is never chosen for you.

updateHighlight.description: "1": this reason goes into the Highlights data module.

allowInvalid.description: With write: true, write even when verification.schema.state is "invalid". Default false.

includeXml.description: Include the XML in the response (default: true when write is false, false when write is true).

tools.name: add_reason_for_update
tools.description: Add ONE reason for update (reasonForUpdate) to the status element of an IN-WORK data module, and nothing else: the content is not touched and no change markup is added. tools.name: extract_segments
tools.description: Take the sentences that a person reads out of a data module so they can be translated: titles, paragraphs, step texts, warnings / cautions / notes, table cells and figure captions. Each segment has a stable id, its XPath, a context hint and the text, with inline elements (emphasis, references …) replaced by {1}, {2} placeholders that must stay in the translation. Attribute values, DMCs, ICNs, applicability expressions and ids are never offered. Also returns the skeletonHash to pass to apply_segments. The server does not translate and does not score translations.

tools.name: apply_segments
tools.description: Put translated sentences back into the data module they were taken from. The output has the same DMC with only the language changed (issueInfo too if given). It stops with error.code "skeleton-mismatch" when the data module changed since extract_segments (skeletonHash). A segment whose id is unknown, duplicated, or whose {n} placeholders do not match is not applied and is listed in unapplied[] (the original sentence stays). The result is verified. Writes only when write is true.

level.description: admonition の種類（admonition では必須）

rows.description: table の行（1 行目が見出し行）

question.description: fault の step の問い。process の if では条件を人が読める文にしたもの

next.description: 同じ DM の step の id（fault では必須）

choices.description: fault の step の答えと次の手順。process の dialog では選択肢

count.description: person の人数（personnel/@numRequired）。man と一緒には使えない

man.description: person を区別する記号（person/@man）。あれば person として書く

personCategoryCode.description: person の区分（値は解釈しない）

skillLevelCode.description: person の技能の水準（列挙のまま渡す）

estimatedTime.description: person の見積もり時間（estimatedTimeUnit が要る）

estimatedTimeUnit.description: 見積もり時間の単位（値は解釈しない）

reqTechInfoCategory.description: document の区分（列挙のまま渡す）

quantity.description: equipment / supply / spare の数量（必須）

unit.description: 数量の単位（値は解釈しない）

partNumber.description: equipment / supply / spare の部品番号

manufacturerCode.description: equipment / supply / spare の製造者のコード（natoStockNumber が無いとき、または partNumber を書くときは必須）

natoStockNumber.description: equipment / supply / spare の NATO 物品番号（NSN）。数字 13 桁。4-2-3-4 桁をハイフンで区切って書ける

DraftAssert.description: 適用性の 1 つの条件（assert）

displayText.description: 人が読む適用性の表示文

andOr.description: assert が 2 件以上のときに必須

DraftDataModule.description: データモジュール 1 件の入力。識別情報（採番の元）、題名、機密区分と内容部の木を持つ

sourceId.description: 採番に使う識別子。dmCode（pm は pmCode）を省いたときに要る。同じ sourceId には同じ DMC を返す

issueDate.description: YYYY-MM-DD。省略時は実行環境の今日の日付

securityClassification.description: 機密区分（列挙のまま。省略を許さない）

responsiblePartnerCompany.description: 責任企業の企業コード。省略時は allocation.icn.cageCode

originator.description: 作成者の企業コード。省略時は allocation.icn.cageCode

InfoCodeSpec.description: 情報コード（意味は付けない）

Allocation.description: 採番の規則。writer は状態を持たず、ledger を入力で受け取り応答で返す

map.description: sourceId → DMC の一部。無い sourceId は rules で決める

disassyCode.description: 指定すると分解コードを連番にしない

infoCodeByKind.description: kind ごとの情報コード。既定は無く、省略した kind を採番すると入力の誤りになる

cageCode.description: ICN の CAGE コード

next.description: 次に使う連番。応答に次の値を返す

ledger.description: sourceId → DMC / PMC、assetId → ICN。前回の応答の ledger をそのまま渡す
